stories.title: Germany: Bundeswehr troop numbers reach 13-year high
stories.summary: Germany's Defense Ministry is reporting a comparatively rare success story in its bid to bolster troop numbers. At the end of July, the total stood at around 186,700, roughly 3,700 more than a year earlier — a 2% boost.

Japan Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said in a social media post that Putin's visit was "absolutely unacceptable" while referring to the islands, which it calls the "Northern Territories" as "inherently Japanese territory." Russia's Foreign Ministry said in response that the islands are an "integral part" of Russia . stories.title: US hiker dies after being struck by lightning on Mount Etna
stories.summary: The 30-year-old was on the active volcano when a thunderstorm developed, local media report.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Mt Etna is Europe's most active volcano, with a series of eruptions occurring in recent weeks By Alex Kleiderman Published 6 hours ago An American tourist has died after being struck by lightning while hiking on Mount Etna in Sicily. The 30-year-old, who has not been named by authorities, was on the active volcano on Sunday when a thunderstorm broke out, Italian media report. The man is said to have been found by firefighters and emergency services in a state of cardiac arrest at about 20:00 local time (18:00 GMT) in a restricted area sometimes used to get closer to the summit. He was flown by helicopter to Cannizzaro Hospital in Catania but was declared dead on arrival. A series of recent eruptions from Europe's most active volcano have caused local air traffic disruption but have also drawn in many tourists. Authorities have been limiting access to more areas of Etna, including the upper slopes where there is little shelter above the tree line, because of the increased volcanic activity. Italy's civil protection agency warns that a combination of volcanic activity and sudden weather changes higher up the mountain can make conditions hazardous.

Without naming him directly, the Metropolitan Police said he was found "unresponsive" in Battersea, south London , and pronounced dead at the scene. "At this time his death is being treated as unexpected, but is not believed to be suspicious," a spokesperson said. "His next-of-kin have been informed and are being supported by officers." Arday, a professor of sociology of education at Cambridge, one of the world's top universities, resigned just over a week ago amid mounting allegations that he plagiarized parts of his PhD thesis and overstated his personal achievements. He had denied wrongdoing, saying in a resignation letter last week that he did not accept "the narratives that have surrounded me."
